identity.name: General Government
native_names: Generalgouvernement für die besetzten polnischen Gebiete
alt_names: General Government for the Occupied Polish Territories

land.text: the part of pre-war Poland German forces held that was neither annexed to the Reich nor taken by the Soviets; the Reich 'had already annexed large parts of western pre-war Poland (8 October 1939)' and the Soviet Union 'taken over 51.6% of the territory of Poland'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Second Polish Republic row ends in 1938/1939; the eu-21 dossier for it owns the 1939 conquest.

land.text: Poland, 'declared restored' on 22 July 1944; 'USSR captures Warsaw: 17 January 1945'; 'Disintegration: 19 January 1945'

successors.note: District Galicia (Lwów, Tarnopol, Stanisławów) went back to the Ukrainian SSR in 1944; the rest of the General Government to the Polish state under Soviet control. Cliopatria's Republic of Poland row begins in 1953 and the eu-22 dossier must cover 1944-1952.

capitals.name: Litzmannstadt (Łódź)
capitals.note: The infobox gives 'Litzmannstadt' from 12 October to 4 November 1939; Łódź itself lay in the Reich's Wartheland, so this was the seat of Frank's first office, not a city of the territory.

rulers.name: Hans Frank
rulers.title: Governor-General
rulers.note: Infobox '1939–1945: Hans Frank'; 'appointed Governor-General of this occupied area on 12 October 1939' (German-occupied Poland page). 'American troops captured Hans Frank ... in May 1945.'

correction.text: 'the Distrikt Warschau, the Distrikt Lublin, the Distrikt Radom, and the Distrikt Krakau' of 26 October 1939, about 94,000 km2: modern Lesser Poland, Lublin, Holy Cross, Subcarpathian and Masovian voivodeships, less the Zichenau district of Masovia (annexed to East Prussia, a 60 km circle around Ciechanów-Płock) and the Oświęcim area (East Upper Silesia, annexed to the Reich)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no shape for the General Government (its Second Polish Republic row stops before the invasion). The German-occupied Poland page says 'initially about 12 million in an area of 94,000 square kilometres'; the resolved spec is about 97,000 km2 (ratio 1.03, fine). The General Government page lists the four districts but gives no area (page silent), and gives 11.4 million inhabitants in December 1939. The modern voivodeships do not follow the 1939 lines: the Zichenau district and the Oświęcim area are cut out by circles, and the Subcarpathian voivodeship includes ground east of the San that the Soviets held.

union.text: 'the Distrikt Warschau, the Distrikt Lublin, the Distrikt Radom, and the Distrikt Krakau' of 26 October 1939, about 94,000 km2: modern Lesser Poland, Lublin, Holy Cross, Subcarpathian and Masovian voivodeships, less the Zichenau district of Masovia (annexed to East Prussia, a 60 km circle around Ciechanów-Płock) and the Oświęcim area (East Upper Silesia, annexed to the Reich)

correction.text: the four districts plus District Galicia, added on 1 August 1941

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for District Galicia (created 1 August 1941): 51,200 km2 and 4,400,000 people on the District of Galicia page against about 50,100 km2 for the gazetteer's Eastern Galicia region (ratio 0.98, fine). Whole General Government about 147,000 km2 resolved; the pages give no total (page silent).

correction.text: what was left of the General Government west of the Vistula-San line in 1944-1945 as an approximation: Kraków, Radom and Warsaw districts; the Lublin district (east of the Vistula) and the Subcarpathian land had passed to Poland (22 July 1944 'Poland declared restored')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the collapse. The page says 'As the Soviets advanced through Poland in late 1944 the General Government collapsed' and dates only 'Poland declared restored: 22 July 1944', the Soviet capture of Warsaw on 17 January 1945 and the disintegration on 19 January 1945. District Galicia was 'retaken by the Soviet Union in 1944' (Galicia page, Wächter's term ended in August 1944). Which towns fell on which day is not on the pages, so the shape west of the Vistula is an approximation; about 53,000 km2 resolved.

region.text: 'the Distrikt Warschau, the Distrikt Lublin, the Distrikt Radom, and the Distrikt Krakau' of 26 October 1939, about 94,000 km2: modern Lesser Poland, Lublin, Holy Cross, Subcarpathian and Masovian voivodeships, less the Zichenau district of Masovia (annexed to East Prussia, a 60 km circle around Ciechanów-Płock) and the Oświęcim area (East Upper Silesia, annexed to the Reich)

ledger.note: 26 October 1939: the General Government is set up for the part of occupied Poland the Reich did not annex. 'A Führer's decree of October 12, 1939 established the General Government; the decree came into force on October 26, 1939'; four districts, 'the Distrikt Warschau, the Distrikt Lublin, the Distrikt Radom, and the Distrikt Krakau'; 'initially about 12 million in an area of 94,000 square kilometres' (German-occupied Poland page).

region.text: the General Government under German civil administration

ledger.note: 26 October 1939: Germany administers the General Government as occupied territory. Hans Frank 'was appointed Governor-General of this occupied area on 12 October 1939'; infobox 'Establishment: 26 October 1939'. The nazi-germany dossier records the same land as occupation of the Polish state.

region.text: the District of Galicia, 'the pre-war Lwów, Tarnopol, and Stanisławów voivodeships', 51,200 km2 and 4,400,000 people

ledger.note: 1 August 1941: the District of Galicia is added after Operation Barbarossa. 'created by Nazi Germany on 1 August 1941 after the start of Operation Barbarossa' and 'incorporated into the General Government'; General Government page: 'The territory was expanded substantially in 1941, after the German invasion of the Soviet Union, to include the new District of Galicia' (infobox 'Galicia added: 1 August 1941'). The land had been Soviet since 1939 'as part of Soviet Ukraine'.

region.text: the Lublin district and the east of the territory, taken by the Red Army and the Polish administration in the summer of 1944 (page silent on the day)

ledger.note: 22 July 1944: Poland is 'declared restored'. The page dates only that declaration (infobox 'Poland declared restored: 22 July 1944') and says 'As the Soviets advanced through Poland in late 1944 the General Government collapsed'; it is silent on when the Lublin district and the land east of the Vistula passed to the Soviet-backed Polish administration. The date is the nearest the pages give.

region.text: the District of Galicia, 'the pre-war Lwów, Tarnopol, and Stanisławów voivodeships', 51,200 km2 and 4,400,000 people

ledger.note: August 1944: District Galicia is lost. 'The region was retaken by the Soviet Union in 1944'; infobox disestablished 1944; the officeholder table puts the end of Otto Wächter's term in August 1944. The page does not date the fall of Lviv.

region.text: what was left of the General Government west of the Vistula-San line in 1944-1945 as an approximation: Kraków, Radom and Warsaw districts; the Lublin district (east of the Vistula) and the Subcarpathian land had passed to Poland (22 July 1944 'Poland declared restored')

ledger.note: 17-19 January 1945: the Red Army takes Warsaw and the General Government disintegrates. 'USSR captures Warsaw: 17 January 1945'; 'Disintegration: 19 January 1945'.

region.text: what was left of the General Government west of the Vistula-San line in 1944-1945 as an approximation: Kraków, Radom and Warsaw districts; the Lublin district (east of the Vistula) and the Subcarpathian land had passed to Poland (22 July 1944 'Poland declared restored')

ledger.note: January 1945: the remainder of the General Government passes to the restored Polish state. 'As the Soviets advanced through Poland in late 1944 the General Government collapsed'; 'Poland declared restored: 22 July 1944'. The pages do not give the Kraków date.

region.text: what was left of the General Government west of the Vistula-San line in 1944-1945 as an approximation: Kraków, Radom and Warsaw districts; the Lublin district (east of the Vistula) and the Subcarpathian land had passed to Poland (22 July 1944 'Poland declared restored')

ledger.note: 19 January 1945: the General Government ends. Infobox 'Disintegration: 19 January 1945'; 'The end of the war saw the USSR occupy all of Poland' (German-occupied Poland page).

wars.name: Operation Barbarossa

zones.text: the District of Galicia, 'the pre-war Lwów, Tarnopol, and Stanisławów voivodeships', 51,200 km2 and 4,400,000 people

wars.outcome: The Wehrmacht overran Soviet-held East Galicia in the first days of the invasion; on 1 August 1941 it became the District of Galicia of the General Government.
wars.note: 'When the Wehrmacht forces invaded the Soviet Union in June 1941 (Operation Barbarossa)... Within days East Galicia was overrun and incorporated into the District of Galicia.' The Operation Barbarossa article itself was not opened (page budget).

certainty.note: The border with the annexed Reich lands follows the October 1939 decrees and the border with the USSR the German-Soviet line of 28 September 1939 ('met again on September 28 to delineate a permanent border'); the pages give no survey, but both were fixed on paper.
The Soviet advance moved the front month by month; the pages date only 22 July 1944, 17 January 1945 and 19 January 1945.

sources.title: General Government

sources.title: German-occupied Poland

sources.title: District of Galicia
sources.note: Created 1 August 1941, 51,200 km2, 4,400,000 people, Lwów/Tarnopol/Stanisławów voivodeships, retaken 1944.

notes: Cliopatria lacks the General Government. The Reich annexations of October 1939 (Wartheland, Danzig-West Prussia, Zichenau, East Upper Silesia, Suwałki) are in the nazi-germany dossier; the pages here name them but do not give areas. Bezirk Białystok is not on the pages and is not in the shape (the nazi-germany dossier gives it to the Byelorussian SSR occupation). The General Government page does not give the 22 June 1941 date, the Lublin advance of July 1944 or the Kraków date of 1945; the 1944 loss of the Lublin district is therefore at confidence 1. The shape of 1944-1945 is an approximation. Region names the gazetteer lacks: none (circles stand in for the Zichenau district and the Oświęcim area, which are real names the gazetteer lacks as places: Ciechanów, Płock, Oświęcim, Mława); a 'Zichenau' region would be better.
